en: Any of various medical instruments used to explore wounds, organs, etc.
An anal probe, a fictional instrument commonly used by aliens on abducted humans.
To explore, investigate, question, test, or prove.
To insert a probe into.

probe.ety:
For verb: borrowed from Latin probare (“to test, examine, prove”), from probus (“good”). Doublet of prove.
For noun: borrowed from Late Latin proba (“a proof”), from probare (“to test, examine, prove”); Doublet of proof. Compare Spanish tienta (“a surgeon's probe”), from tentar (“try, test”); see tempt.

ex.en: Investigators are running a probe into what caused the crash.
ex.ja: 調査団は墜落の原因について綿密な調査を行っています。

note.ja: ラテン語 probare（試す）から。試し調べる →「探る・調査（する）・探査機」。prove と同じ。

en: Forbidden; banned; unallowed.

ex.en: Religious education is prohibited at a public school.
ex.ja: 公立学校では宗教教育が禁止されている。

ex.en: Recently, more and more countries have prohibited smoking.
ex.ja: 最近喫煙を禁止する国が増えている。

ex.en: My parents prohibited me from seeing Tom again.
ex.ja: 両親は私がまたトムと会うことを禁止した。

note.ja: prohibit（禁じる）+ -ed。pro（前で）+ habere（持つ・保つ）。「前に立って押しとどめる」→「禁止する」。habit も同じ habere。

en: Occurring once every quarter year (three months); taking place quarter-yearly.
(of a coat of arms) Divided into four parts crosswise.
A periodical publication that appears four times per year.
Once every quarter year (three months).
In the four, or in two diagonally opposite, quarters of a shield.

ex.ja: 四半期１．２％の成長は年率４．９％の成長率を意味する。

ex.en: When annualized, the quarterly gain represents a 4% growth.
ex.ja: 年率に換算すると、この四半期の増加は４％の成長になる。

note.ja: quarter（4分の1）+ -ly。ラテン語 quartus（4番目）。「年の4分の1ごとに」→「四半期の・季刊の」。

en: A supply of anything wasted or exhausted; a reinforcement.
A person enlisted for service in the army; a newly enlisted soldier.
To enroll or enlist new members or potential employees on behalf of an employer, organization, sports team, the military, etc.
To supply with new men, as an army; to fill up or make up by enlistment; also, to muster

ex.en: Our basketball team is recruiting tall boys.
ex.ja: うちのバスケット部は背の高い男子を募集している。

ex.en: Hey, the new recruit this time seems really cute.
ex.ja: おい、今度の新人かわいいらしいぜ。

ex.en: The captain exercised the new recruits with long marches.
ex.ja: 隊長は長時間行進させて新兵たちを訓練した。

note.ja: フランス語 recroître（再び育つ）から。re + crescere（育つ）。「新しく育ってくる兵」→「新兵・募集する」。increase、crescent も同じ crescere。

en: The process of rehabilitating somebody or something.

rehabilitation.ety: From Middle French réhabilitation, from Medieval Latin rehabilitatio.

ex.en: He came to take a walk every morning after rehabilitation.
ex.ja: 彼はリハビリの後、毎朝散歩するようになりました。

ex.en: Half-hearted cutbacks that can't save money leave JAL's rehabilitation in doubt.
ex.ja: コストダウンもできない生ぬるいリストラがJAL再建を危うくする。

note.ja: re（再び）+ habilitare（能力を与える）+ -ation。ラテン語 habilis（扱いやすい・有能な）。「再び能力を取り戻させること」→「リハビリ・社会復帰」。ability と同じ。

en: A rearrangement of an older piece of music, possibly including various cosmetic changes.
A piece of music formed by combining existing pieces of music together, possibly including various other cosmetic changes
To mix again.
To create a remix.

remix.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Italic *wre-
Latin re-der.
Old French re-bor.
Middle English re-
English re-
English mix
English remix
From re- + mix.

ex.en: The DJ played a remix of a popular song.
ex.ja: そのＤＪは人気曲のリミックスをかけた。

note.ja: re（再び）+ mix（混ぜる）。「もう一度ミックスし直すこと」。

en: A person who resists; especially a member of a resistance movement.
A thing which resists.
Which makes resistance or offers opposition.
Which is not affected or overcome by a disease, drug, chemical or atmospheric agent, extreme of temperature, etc.

resistant.ety: From French résistant; equivalent to resist + -ant.

ex.en: The viola is a cold-resistant plant.
ex.ja: ビオラは耐寒性植物だよ。

ex.en: The viola is a plant resistant to the cold.
ex.ja: ビオラは耐寒性植物だよ。

ex.en: This car is resistant to rust.
ex.ja: この車は錆に強い。

note.ja: resist（抵抗する）+ -ant。re（逆らって）+ sistere（立つ）。「逆らって立つ」→「抵抗力のある」。

en: Any rotating cylindrical device that is part of a machine, especially one used to apply or reduce pressure.
A cylindrical (or approximately cylindrical) item used under a heavy object to facilitate moving it; usually several are needed.
To roller skate.

roller.ety:
* From Middle English rollere, equivalent to roll + -er.
* (credits in TV or film): These were originally printed on a physical cylinder that was rotated in front of the camera.

ex.en: Can we roller-skate in this park?
ex.ja: この公園でローラースケートをしてもいいですか。

ex.en: I got the roller skates for nothing.
ex.ja: 私はそのローラースケートをただで手に入れた。

ex.en: Show her how to roller skate.
ex.ja: 彼女にローラースケートの仕方を教えてやりなさい。

note.ja: roll（転がる）+ -er。roll はラテン語 rota（車輪）の縮小 rotula から。rotate（回転する）と同じ。

en: Thin, generally in a negative sense (as opposed to slim, which is thin in a positive sense).
Of food or a beverage, having reduced fat or calories.
The details or facts; especially, those obtained by gossip or rumor.
A state of nakedness; nudity.
To reduce or cut down.

skinny.ety: From Middle English skinny (“resembling skin”), equivalent to skin + -y. The meaning associated with lack of fat or muscle possibly derives from the phrase skin and bones; the meaning associated with nudity refers to the exposed skin.

ex.en: That man is skinny, but his wife is fat.
ex.ja: その男はやせているが、彼の妻は太っている。

ex.en: The dog is brown, small, and skinny.
ex.ja: 茶色くて、小さくて、やせっぽちの犬です。

ex.en: It's more polite to say thin than skinny.
ex.ja: 「痩せている」と言うよりも「細い」と言った方が失礼に当たりません。

note.ja: skin（皮膚）+ -y。「皮ばかりの」→「やせこけた」。

en: One who sneaks; one who moves stealthily to acquire an item or information.
The act of sneaking
To creep or go stealthily; to come or go while trying to avoid detection, as a person who does not wish to be seen.
To take (something) in a surreptitious manner, so as to avoid being noticed.
In advance; before release to the general public.
In a stealthy or surreptitious manner.

sneak.ety: Possibly from Middle English sniken (“to creep, crawl”), from Old English snīcan (“to creep, crawl”), from Proto-West Germanic *snīkan, from Proto-Germanic *snīkaną (“to creep, crawl”), of sound-symbolic origin; compare formally unrelated snake, snoop, snook, snoke, and snoot. Cognate with Danish snige (“to sneak”), Swedish snika (“to sneak, hanker after”), Icelandic sníkja (“to sneak, hanker after”). Possibly related to snitch.

ex.en: I caught him trying to sneak out.
ex.ja: 私は彼が忍び出ようとするのをつかまえた。

ex.en: May I sneak in? My flight is leaving soon.
ex.ja: 通していただけますか。飛行機が出ちゃいますので。

ex.en: I noticed him sneak into the room.
ex.ja: 彼が部屋に忍び込むのに気がついた。

note.ja: 古英語 snīcan（はう・こっそり進む）から。「こっそり動く」。sneakers（音のしない靴）。

en: Causing pain or discomfort; painfully sensitive.
Sensitive; tender; easily pained, grieved, or vexed; very susceptible of irritation.
Sorely.
An injured, infected, inflamed or diseased patch of skin.
Grief; affliction; trouble; difficulty.
To mutilate the legs or feet of (a horse) in order to induce a particular gait.
To grow sores; to be beset with skin lesions.

sore.ety:
From Middle English sor, from Old English sār (“ache, wound”, noun) and sār (“painful, grievous”, adjective), from Proto-West Germanic *sair, from Proto-Germanic *sairaz (adjective) from Proto-Indo-European *seh₂iro-, enlargement of *seh₂y- (“to be fierce, afflict”).
See also Dutch zeer (“sore, ache”), Danish sår (“wound”), German sehr (“very”); also Hittite [script needed] (sāwar, “anger”), Welsh hoed (“pain”), Ancient Greek αἱμωδία (haimōdía, “sensation of having teeth on edge”).

ex.en: She was sore at me for being late.
ex.ja: 私が遅刻したので彼女は怒った。

ex.en: I'm still a bit sore after my operation.
ex.ja: 手術を終えて私はまだ少し痛い。

ex.en: I am still a bit sore after my operation.
ex.ja: 手術を終えて私はまだ少し痛い。

note.ja: 古英語 sār（痛み）から。ドイツ語 sehr（とても）と同系。「痛い・ひりひりする」。

en: A small particle of glowing matter, either molten or on fire, resulting from an electrical surge or excessive heat created by friction.
A short or small burst of electrical discharge.
To trigger, kindle into activity (an argument, etc).
To light; to kindle.

en: The process or act of thinking or meditating on a subject.
The act or process of reasoning a priori from premises given or assumed.

speculation.ety: From Middle English speculacioun, speculation, from Old French speculation (compare French spéculation), from Late Latin speculātiō, speculātiōnem, from Latin speculor. Morphologically speculate + -ion.

ex.en: He lost the greater part of his fortune in speculation.
ex.ja: 彼は投機に手を出して財産の大半を失った。

ex.en: No speculation has taken place concerning the motives.
ex.ja: 動機についてはまったく考察されていない。

ex.en: Speculation is growing apace.
ex.ja: いろんな予想が飛び交っていますね。

note.ja: spec（見る）+ ulat + ion。見張り台から見ること →「推測・投機」。speculate（推測する）。

Expensive.
The steep side of a mountain etc.; a slope or acclivity.
To soak or wet thoroughly.
To make tea (or other beverages) by soaking leaves in water, which flavors the water.

ex.ja: ティーバッグを熱湯の中に入れました。

en: A dried stalk of a cereal plant.
Such dried stalks considered collectively; this bulk matter may be a chief salable product, a by-product, fodder, bedding, or green manur…
Made of straw.
Of a pale, yellowish beige colour, like that of a dried straw.
To scatter or to spread loosely.
To lay straw around plants to protect them from frost.

ex.ja: 私はこの古い麦藁帽子にとても愛着がある。

en: A person or thing that immediately follows another in holding an office or title.
The next heir in order or succession.

successor.ety: From Anglo-Norman successour, from Latin successor.

ex.en: The matter of his successor is still under debate.
ex.ja: 彼の後継者についての問題はまだ論争中だ。

note.ja: suc（次に）+ cess（進む）+ or（人）。後に続く人 →「後継者」。

en: Not certain; unsure.
Not known for certain; questionable.
Something uncertain; everything uncertain.

uncertain.ety: From Middle English uncerteyn. By surface analysis, un- + certain.

ex.en: I am uncertain when he will come next.
ex.ja: 彼が今度いつ来るかはっきりとは知らない。

ex.en: It was uncertain whether he would marry her.
ex.ja: 彼が彼女と結婚するかどうかは確かではなかった。

ex.en: The weather is uncertain at this time of year.
ex.ja: 今ごろの天気は当てにならない。

note.ja: un（否定）+ certain（確かな）。「確かではない」。certain はラテン語 cernere（ふるい分ける）から。

en: To transfer data to a computer on a network, especially to a server on the Internet.
To transfer jurisdiction and responsibility of a government asset or service to a higher level of government.
Such a file transfer.

ex.en: I can't figure out how to upload an image.
ex.ja: 画像のアップロードの仕方が分かりません。

ex.en: We uploaded the pictures from our wedding to Facebook.
ex.ja: 私達はフェイスブックに結婚の写真をアップロードしました。

ex.en: I make, and upload, Japanese video lessons to YouTube.
ex.ja: 私はYouTubeで日本語の動画レッスンを作ってアップしています。

note.ja: up（上へ）+ load（積む）。「（データを）上のサーバーへ積み上げる」→「アップロード」。download の反対。

Any member of a (generalized) vector space.
To set (particularly an aircraft) on a course toward a selected point.
To redirect to a vector, or code entry point.

Often with "out", to measure a certain amount of something by its weight, e.g. for sale.
The act of weighing, of measuring the weight

ex.ja: 彼は肉を切り刻んで重さを量った。

ex.en: The baby weighed seven pounds at birth.
ex.ja: その赤ん坊は生まれた時体重は七ポンドでした。

en: Whatever.
In any way; at all; whatever.

whatsoever.ety: From Middle English whatsoever. By surface analysis, what + so + -ever.

ex.en: There was no warning whatsoever.
ex.ja: 警告は全くなかった。

ex.en: Is there any hope whatsoever?
ex.ja: 少しは希望があるのか。

ex.en: Tom has no interest whatsoever in being fashionably dressed.
ex.ja: トムはおしゃれに全く関心がない。

note.ja: what + so + ever。whatever を強めた形。否定文で「少しも〜ない」。

en: Evil or mischievous by nature; morally reprehensible.
Harsh; severe.
Wicked (evil) people collectively.

Not existing.
Something absent, especially absent people collectively; those who were or are not there.
In the absence of; without; except.
To keep (oneself) away.

A medicine or other agent to assist hearing.

en: Conditions suitable for an organism or population of organisms to live.

habitat.ety: From Latin habitat (“it dwells, lives”), the 3rd person singular present active indicative form of habitō (“to live or dwell”). Compare the English derivations of exit, floruit, ignoramus, and tenet from Latin finite verbs reanalyzed as English nouns.

ex.en: The vase arrived intact despite the long trip.
ex.ja: 長旅にもかかわらず、花びんは無傷で届いた。

note.ja: ラテン語 intactus ＝ in（否定）+ tangere（触れる）。「触れられていない」→「無傷の」。tangible、contact と同じ。

en: The place where water, air or other fluid is taken into a pipe or conduit; opposed to outlet.
The beginning of a contraction or narrowing in a tube or cylinder.
To take in or draw in; to bring in from outside.

intake.ety: From English dialectal (Northern England/Scotland), deverbal of take in, equivalent to in- + take. More at in-, take.

ex.en: You won't lose weight unless you cut back on your food intake.
ex.ja: ごはんの量を減らさなければ、痩せません。

ex.en: After his heart attack, Jim had to cut down on his sugar intake.
ex.ja: 心臓発作の後、ジムは砂糖の摂取量をへらさなければならなかった。

ex.en: Please limit your fluid intake.
ex.ja: 水分を控えてください。

note.ja: in（中に）+ take（取る）。「中に取り込むこと」→「摂取（量）・取り入れ口」。

en: Not relevant, as
Not at all related: totally unrelated, wholly unconnected, completely inapplicable.

irrelevant.ety:

Proto-Indo-European *n̥-
Proto-Italic *n̥-
Latin in-
Latin ir-
English ir-
English relevant
English irrelevant
From ir- + relevant.

ex.en: What he said is irrelevant to the matter.
ex.ja: 彼の言ったことはその問題に関係ない。

ex.en: Can I ask you something completely irrelevant?
ex.ja: ちょっと全然関係ないこと聞いてもいい？

ex.en: Your suggestion seems irrelevant to our discussion here.
ex.ja: あなたの提案はここの議論とは無関係のように思われます。

note.ja: ir（否定）+ relevant（関連のある）。relevant はラテン語 relevare（持ち上げる・助けになる）から。「役に立つ → 関係がある」の否定。relieve と同じ。

en: One of the bones, usually bearing teeth, which form the framework of the mouth.
The part of the face below the mouth.
To assail or abuse by scolding.
To scold; to clamor.

jaw.ety:
From Middle English jawe/jowe (“jaw; sides of the lower face”, 14th century), the further origin of which is disputed. Either:
* From Anglo-Norman jowe, from Old French joe (“cheek; jaw”), from Vulgar Latin *ga(v)ota (“cheek”), of uncertain further origin.
** It has been objected that the rhyming of jowe (“jaw”) with clowe (“claw”) in Middle English demonstrates that it did not have the vowel /uː/. This would be a concern if /uː/ were the vowel to expect from a borrowing of the Old French word, which it is not. Compare English paw < Middle English pawe/powe < Anglo-Norman powe < Old French poe

ex.en: When I heard about it, my jaw dropped.
ex.ja: 聞いた時、開いた口が塞がらなかったよ。

ex.en: He got a broken jaw and lost some teeth.
ex.ja: 彼は顎の骨を折って、歯も何本か折れた。

ex.en: As his eyes ran over the paper, his jaw fell.
ex.ja: 一通り読み終えたところで、あんぐり口を開けた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 joue（頬）からとされる。「あご」。

en: A young cat; a kitten.
An adult cat; also (often childish), sometimes in the form Kitty: a pet name for a cat of any age.

kitty.ety:
From kitt(en) + -y (diminutive suffix). Compare Dutch katje (“kitty”).
Etymology 1 sense 2 (“vulva and/or vagina”) is probably modelled after the use of pussy to refer to the body part, from the appearance of an unshaven vulva.

ex.en: I have a kitty and a dog.
ex.ja: 子猫と犬を飼ってます。

ex.en: I want a Hello Kitty pencil board.
ex.ja: キティちゃんの下敷きが欲しい。

ex.en: That's not for kitties!
ex.ja: それは子猫のためじゃないよ。

note.ja: kit（kitten の短縮）+ -y。子猫を呼ぶ愛称。kitten は cat の縮小形。

en: Ground (generally in front of or around a house) covered with grass kept closely mown.
An open space between woods.
To furnish with a lawn.

ex.en: I had my son water the lawn.
ex.ja: 私は息子に芝生に水を撒かせた。

ex.en: They are sitting on the lawn and the ground.
ex.ja: 芝生や地面に座っている。

ex.en: Bob charged 3 dollars an hour for mowing lawns.
ex.ja: ボブは芝刈りに１時間３ドルを請求した。

note.ja: 古フランス語 launde（森の中の空き地）から。「草地」→「芝生」。

en: A long, thin, sharp implement usually for piercing as in sewing, embroidery, acupuncture, tattooing, body piercing, medical injections, s…
Any slender, pointed object resembling a needle, such as a pointed crystal, a sharp pinnacle of rock, an obelisk, etc.
To pierce with a needle, especially for sewing or acupuncture.
To tease in order to provoke; to poke fun at.

ex.ja: 針と糸を持っていませんか。

ex.ja: ちょっとこの針に糸通してくれない？

ex.en: He hurt his finger with a needle.
ex.ja: 彼は針で指を刺した。

note.ja: 古英語 nǣdl から。ドイツ語 Nadel と同じ。「縫う道具」が原義とされる。

en: A two-dimensional one.
A three-dimensional one.
Having the shape of an oval.
Of or pertaining to an ovum.

ex.ja: 卵は、真ん丸ではなく楕円です。

ex.en: Especially remarkable was her oval face.
ex.ja: とりわけ人目をひいたのは、彼女の卵型の顔立ちだった。

ex.en: The stirrup rests on the oval window of the inner ear.
ex.ja: アブミ骨は内耳の前庭窓に接している。

note.ja: ラテン語 ovum（卵）から。「卵の形の」→「楕円形の」。

en: A feeling of sympathy at the misfortune or suffering of someone or something.
Feeling of contempt one has for someone who is hopelessly inferior.
To feel pity for (someone or something).
To feel contempt for someone who is hopelessly inferior.

pity.ety: From Middle English pitye, pitie, pittye, pitee, pite, from Anglo-Norman pité, pittee etc., from Old French pitet, pitié, from Latin pietās. See also the doublets pietà and piety.

ex.en: It's a pity that you should leave Japan.
ex.ja: 君が日本を離れるのは残念だ。

ex.en: It is a pity that he can't come.
ex.ja: 彼が来れないのは残念だ。

ex.en: I do think that it is a pity.
ex.ja: 本当に残念だと思う。

note.ja: ラテン語 pietas（敬虔・義務感）から。piety（敬虔）と同じ語源で、後に意味が分かれた。

en: An inland body of standing water, either natural or man-made, that is smaller than a lake.
An inland body of standing water of any size that is fed by springs rather than by a river.
To block the flow of water so that it can escape only through evaporation or seepage; to dam.
To make into a pond; to collect, as water, in a pond by damming.

pond.ety: From Middle English pond, ponde (“pond, pool”), probably from Old English *pond, *pand (attested in placenames), a variant of *pund (“enclosure”). Doublet of pound.

ex.en: There used to be a pond around here.
ex.ja: 以前このあたりに池があった。

ex.en: This pond doesn't run dry even in summer.
ex.ja: この池は夏でも干上がらない。

ex.en: There is a small pond in our garden.
ex.ja: うちの庭には小さな池がある。

note.ja: pound（家畜の囲い）と同じ語。「水をせき止めて囲った所」→「池」。

en: A person who carries luggage and related objects; (historically) one who carried luggage or did manual labour in the transloading of cargo.
An ant having the specialized role of carrying.
To serve as a porter; to carry.

porter.ety: From Middle English porter, portere, portier, borrowed from Anglo-Norman portour and Old French porteor, from Late Latin portātor, from past participle of Latin portāre (“to carry”). By surface analysis, port (“to carry”) + -er.

ex.en: Porters often have to walk across the tracks.
ex.ja: ポーターはしばしば線路を歩いて渡らなければならない。

ex.en: I had the porter carry my suitcase.
ex.ja: 私は赤帽にスーツケースを運んでもらった。

ex.en: She had her heavy suitcase carried by the porter.
ex.ja: 彼女は重いスーツケースをポーターに運んでもらった。

note.ja: port（運ぶ）+ er（人）。荷物を運ぶ人 →「荷物運搬人・ポーター」。

en: That which is or may be seized by animals to be devoured.
A person or thing given up as a victim.
To act as a predator.

prey.ety: From Middle English preye, prei, preyȝe, borrowed from Anglo-Norman and Old French preie, one of the variants of proie, from Latin praeda. Compare predator. Doublet of prede.

ex.en: Some large birds prey upon small birds and animals.
ex.ja: 大きな鳥は小鳥や小動物を捕って食べるものもいる。

ex.en: The number of prey they killed was the same.
ex.ja: 彼らが殺したえじきの数はおなじだった。

ex.en: The old woman fell an easy prey to the fraud.
ex.ja: その老婦人はまんまと詐欺師の餌食となった。

note.ja: ラテン語 praeda（獲物・戦利品）から。predator（捕食者）、depredation（略奪）も同じ。pray（祈る）とは別語。

en: Someone who speaks by divine inspiration.
Someone who predicts the future; a soothsayer.

prophet.ety: From Middle English prophete, from Anglo-Norman prophete, from Latin prophēta, from Ancient Greek προφήτης (prophḗtēs, “one who speaks for a god”), from πρό (pró, “before”) + φημί (phēmí, “to tell”). Displaced native Old English wītga.

ex.en: Once in a while, the prophet indulges in fantasy.
ex.ja: たまに、その預言者は空想にふける。

ex.en: Are you the prophet?
ex.ja: あなたは預言者ですか。

ex.en: Prophets have been forecasting the end of the world for centuries.
ex.ja: 預言者は何世紀もの間、この世の終わりを予言し続けてきた。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 prophētēs から。pro（前に・代わりに）+ phanai（話す）。「神に代わって前もって語る人」→「預言者」。prophecy（予言）。

en: A direct popular vote on a proposed law or constitutional amendment.
An action, choice, etc., which is perceived as passing judgment on another matter.

referendum.ety: From Latin referendum (“that which ought to be announced”), from refero (“to announce”).

ex.en: The government put the question to the people in a referendum.
ex.ja: 政府が住民に問う一般投票を実施しました。

ex.en: Kilby applied Emmet's theory to his investigation of the referendum held in Greece in 1948.
ex.ja: キルビーは１９４８年のギリシャ国民投票にエメット理論を適用した。

note.ja: ラテン語 referre（持ち帰る・付託する）の動名詞。「国民に持ち帰って判断を委ねること」→「国民投票」。refer と同じ。

en: To dictate policy.
To control or direct according to rule, principle, or law.

regulate.ety: Borrowed from Latin regulatus, perfect passive participle of regulō (“to direct, rule, regulate”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from regula (“rule”), from regō (“to keep straight, direct, govern, rule”). Compare regle, rail. Displaced native Old English metegian.

ex.en: Traffic lights are used to regulate traffic.
ex.ja: 交通信号は交通の流れを規制するために使われている。

ex.en: Hong Kong is the least regulated economy in Asia.
ex.ja: 香港はアジアでは最も規制が少ない経済である。

ex.en: Rice prices are regulated by the government.
ex.ja: 米価は政府によって統制されている。

note.ja: ラテン語 regula（定規・規則）から。reg（まっすぐ）。定規に合わせる →「規制する・調整する」。regular（規則的な）、rule（規則）も同じ。

en: A clear, deep, red variety of corundum, valued as a precious stone.
A deep red colour.
Of a deep, red color; ruby-red.
To make red; to redden.

ruby.ety:
From Middle English ruby, rube, from Old French rubi, from Medieval Latin rubīnus. Doublet of rubi and rubine.
Etymology 1 sense 7 (“pronunciation guide”) is from the British 5½-point type size (etymology 1 sense 6), used for annotations in printed documents.

ex.en: The queen's crown was decorated with rubies.
ex.ja: 女王の王冠はルビーで飾られていた。

note.ja: ラテン語 rubeus（赤い）から。ruber（赤）。rubella（風疹：赤い発疹）も同じ。日本語の「ルビ（振り仮名）」は、昔の印刷で振り仮名に使う活字の大きさの名前（ruby）から。

Appropriate to the season.
Anything that is seasonal, such as a financial trend, a product for sale, or an employee.

ex.ja: それにしても、幼稚園というところは、季節の行事にとても敏感です。

en: Acting with or showing good sense; able to make good judgements based on reason or wisdom, or reflecting such ability.
Characterized more by usefulness, practicality, or comfort than by attractiveness, formality, or fashionableness, especially of clothing.

sensible.ety: From Latin sēnsibilis (“perceptible by the senses, having feeling, sensible”), from sentiō (“to feel, perceive”).

ex.en: What he says sounds very sensible to me.
ex.ja: 彼が言っていることは非常にもっともなことだ、と私には思われる。

ex.en: Ben, if anything, was a sensible man.
ex.ja: ベンはどちらかと言えば分別のある人だった。

ex.en: Ben, if anything, is a sensible man.
ex.ja: ベンはどちらかといえば分別のある男だ。

note.ja: sens（感じる）+ ible。分別をもって感じ取れる →「分別のある・賢明な」。※ sensitive（敏感な）と区別。

en: A narrative that is written after another narrative set in the same universe, especially a narrative that is chronologically set after it…
Synonym of postquel; a narrative work that follows-on and is set after an prior existing work.

sequel.ety: From Middle English sequele, sequelle, sequile, from Middle French sequele, sequelle and its etymon, Latin sequēla, from sequī (“to follow”). Doublet of sequela.

ex.en: By the way, I plan to do that for this story's sequel.
ex.ja: ちなみに、それはこの話の後日談にする予定です。

ex.en: Each sequel of this game contains fewer and fewer characters.
ex.ja: このゲーム、続編が出るたびにキャラが減ってるな。

note.ja: ラテン語 sequi（続く）から。sequ + el。後に続くもの →「続編・結果」。

ex.ja: チームのメンバーを信頼しています。

ex.ja: こちらは、チームメイトのドノヴァンです。

note.ja: team + mate（仲間）。「チームの仲間」。classmate、roommate と同じ作り。

en: The territory of a town.
A subdivision of a county.

township.ety: From Middle English towneship, townschip, tounshipe, tunscipe, from Old English tūnsċipe (“the inhabitants of a town; township”), equivalent to town + -ship.

ex.en: He grew up in a small farming township.
ex.ja: 彼は小さな農村の郡区で育った。

note.ja: town（町）+ -ship。「町区」。

en: Any large cetacean, usually with the exclusion of dolphins and porpoises.
Any species of Cetacea, including dolphins and porpoises.
To hunt for whales.

ex.en: We are having a whale of a time.
ex.ja: 気分は最高。

ex.en: Never have I seen such a big whale.
ex.ja: あんなに大きな鯨、見たことがない。

ex.en: Blue whales are the largest animals on earth.
ex.ja: シロナガスクジラが、地球上で一番大きい動物です。

note.ja: 古英語 hwæl から。ドイツ語 Wal と同じ。

en: To regard with wonder and delight.
To look upon with an elevated feeling of pleasure, as something which calls out approbation, esteem, love or reverence.

admire.ety: From Middle English admyren, borrowed from Middle French admirer, from Latin admīror, from ad + mīror (“wonder at”).

ex.en: Yes. Everyone admires the pictures painted by him.
ex.ja: うん。みんなが彼の描く絵をほめているね。

ex.en: No one admires him more than I do.
ex.ja: 私ほど彼に敬服しているものはありません。

ex.en: They admired the fine view from the hill.
ex.ja: 彼らはその丘からの素晴らしい眺めに感嘆した。

note.ja: ad（〜に）+ mirari（驚く・不思議がる）。「驚嘆して見つめる」→「感心する・称賛する」。miracle（奇跡）、mirror（鏡）も同じ。

en: A hard, generally yellow to brown translucent or transparent fossil resin from extinct coniferous trees of the pine genus, used for jewel…
A yellow-orange colour.
Of a brownish yellow colour, like that of most amber.

amber.ety:
From Middle English ambre, aumbre, from Old French aumbre, ambre, from Arabic عَنْبَر (ʕanbar, “ambergris”), from Middle Persian 𐭠𐭭𐭡𐭫 (ʾnbl /⁠ambar⁠/, “ambergris”). Compare English lamber, ambergris. ex.en: Traffic lights have three colours: red, amber and green.
ex.ja: 信号機は「赤・黄・青」の3色です。

ex.en: Transcending time, the insects of ages gone past dance livelily in amber.
ex.ja: 時を超えて古代の昆虫たちが琥珀の中で生き生きと踊る。

ex.en: "When they say your pee is amber-colored, that means you're dehydrated."
ex.ja: 「小便が琥珀色だと言われたら、脱水症状だ」

note.ja: アラビア語 ʿanbar（龍涎香）から。のちに似た色の化石樹脂を指すようになった。

To cyclically angle the foot at the ankle while pedaling, to maximize the amount of work applied to the pedal during each revolution.

ex.ja: トムはラグビーの試合中に左足首を骨折した。

ex.en: That's when I injured my ankle.
ex.ja: その時に足を痛めたんだ。

note.ja: 古英語 ancleow から。「曲がる所」が原義で、angle（角）と同系とされる。

en: A protective layer over a body, vehicle, or other object intended to deflect or diffuse damaging forces.
A natural form of this kind of protection on an animal's body.
To equip something with armor or a protective coating or hardening.
To provide something with an analogous form of protection.

ex.ja: そこで、旅をするときは、私は鎧をつけることはしません。

ex.en: He who wears armor falls with a big crash!
ex.ja: 鎧をつけている人は、転ぶと大きな音がする。

ex.en: Now we have enough iron to craft some armor for the both of us.
ex.ja: 私たち２人分の防具をつくるために必要な鉄が手に入った。

en: Autism spectrum disorder, a condition characterized by impairment in social communication and interaction, as well as a need or strong pr…

autism.ety: Borrowed from German Autismus, coined by Swiss psychiatrist Eugen Bleuler, first usage dated to 1907 attributed by Carl Jung as an alternative of his for "auto-erotism", although Bleuler himself differentiates the terms in his book Dementia Praecox, first published 1911. From Ancient Greek αὐτός (autós, “self”) + -ισμός (-ismós, “-ism”).

ex.en: Her brother has autism and loves trains.
ex.ja: 彼女の弟は自閉症で、電車が大好きだ。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 autos（自分）+ -ism。「自分の中に閉じこもる状態」として名づけられた。automatic（自ら動く）も同じ autos。

en: A person, especially a man, who is socially regarded as able to marry but has not yet.
A bachelor apartment.

bachelor.ety: From Middle English bacheler, from Anglo-Norman and Old French bacheler (modern French bachelier), from Medieval Latin baccalārius, baccalāris (compare Tuscan baccalare (“squire”)).

ex.en: He remained a bachelor all his life.
ex.ja: 彼は生涯独身のままだった。

ex.en: Tom remained a bachelor until his death.
ex.ja: トムは死ぬまで独身だった。

ex.en: Tom was a bachelor all his life.
ex.ja: トムは生涯独身を貫いた。

note.ja: 中世ラテン語 baccalarius（若い騎士見習い）から。「見習い」→ 大学の最初の学位 →「学士」、まだ一人前に所帯を持たない →「独身男性」。

en: A small succulent fruit, of any one of many varieties.
A soft fruit which develops from a single ovary and contains seeds not encased in pits.
To pick berries.
To bear or produce berries.

berry.ety:

Proto-West Germanic *baʀi

Middle English berie
English berry
From Middle English berie, from Old English berġe, from Proto-West Germanic *baʀi, from Proto-Germanic *bazją.
Cognate with Saterland Frisian Bäie, West Flemish beier, German Beere, Icelandic ber, Danish bær.
The slang sense "police car" may come from the lights on the vehicles' roofs.

ex.en: This berry is good to eat.
ex.ja: この実はたべられます。

ex.en: I brought you some berries.
ex.ja: 苺を持ってきたよ。

ex.en: I love all berries, but especially strawberries.
ex.ja: 私は全ての苺類が好きですが、特にストロベリーが好きです。

note.ja: 古英語 berie から。ゲルマン系の語で、strawberry、blueberry に含まれる。

en: An act of intimidating a person to do something, especially such repeated coercion.
Persistent acts intended to make life unpleasant for another person.

From bully + -ing.

ex.en: That big boy is bullying the little children.
ex.ja: あの大きな男の子は小さな子供達をいじめている。

ex.en: Any sort of bullying is not OK.
ex.ja: いじめは絶対にダメだよ！

ex.en: Any kind of bullying is not okay.
ex.ja: いじめは絶対にダメだよ！

note.ja: bully（いじめっ子）+ -ing。bully はもとオランダ語 boel（恋人・兄弟）で、意味が「威張り散らす人」へ悪化した。

en: A socio-economic system based on private ownership of resources, and capital and their exploitation for profit.
An economic system based on private control of the means of production and the exploitation of labour by capital.

ex.en: They ended capitalism and built a socialist society.
ex.ja: 彼らは資本主義にピリオドを打ち社会主義社会を建設した。

ex.en: Capitalism is the exploitation of man by man. Communism is the exact opposite.
ex.ja: 資本主義とは人間による人間の搾取である。共産主義はその真逆だ。

ex.en: As communism has collapsed, capitalism is now accused of trying to "dominate the world."
ex.ja: 共産主義が崩壊したことにより、今や資本主義が「世界を支配」しようとしているという非難を浴びている。

note.ja: capital（資本）+ -ism。capital はラテン語 caput（頭）から。「（家畜の）頭数」→「財産・資本」。

en: Prudence when faced with, or when expecting to face, danger; care taken in order to avoid risk or harm.
A careful attention to the probable effects of an act, in order that failure or harm may be avoided.
To warn; to alert, advise that caution is warranted.
To read someone their formal legal rights as part of a lawful arrest.

caution.ety: Recorded since 1297 as Middle English caucioun (“bail, guarantee, pledge”), from Old French caution (“security, surety”), itself from Latin cautiō, from cautus, past participle of caveō, cavēre (“be on one's guard”).

ex.en: Caution: risk of electric shock. Do not open.
ex.ja: あけるな危険。感電の可能性あり。

ex.en: I repeat it by way of caution.
ex.ja: 念のためもう一度いいます。

ex.en: The soldiers headed for the frontier with caution.
ex.ja: 兵士達は警戒しながら国境に向かって進んだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 cavere（用心する）から。「用心」→「注意・警告」。precaution（予防措置）も同じ。

en: The act of certifying.
The granting of a certificate.

ex.en: I've been spending a lot of time studying for IT certifications recently.
ex.ja: 最近はほとんどいつもIT関連の検定試験を受けようと勉強しています。

note.ja: certify（証明する）+ -ation。certus（確かな）+ facere（する）。「確かなものとすること」→「証明・認定」。

en: A group of people all descended from a common ancestor, in fact or belief, especially when the exact genealogies are not known.
A traditional social group of families in the Scottish Highlands having a common hereditary chieftain.

clan.ety: Borrowed from Irish clann (“offspring, children of the family”) and Scottish Gaelic clann, both from Old Irish cland, borrowed from Old Welsh plant, itself borrowed from Latin planta (“shoot, offspring”). Doublet of plant and planta.

ex.en: These figures are signs of a family or clan.
ex.ja: これらは一家族あるいは一族を表すものである。

ex.en: Clans run wild like a storm in a raging sea.
ex.ja: 猛り狂う海の嵐のように一族が激しく走る。

ex.en: Recite the names of the members of the Tokugawa clan.
ex.ja: 徳川家の系図を列挙しなさい。

note.ja: スコットランド・ゲール語 clann（子孫）から。ラテン語 planta（若枝）にさかのぼる。「同じ祖先の子孫」→「一族・氏族」。

en: A loud sound, like the crashing together of metal objects; a crash.
A skirmish, a hostile encounter.
To make a clashing sound.
To cause to make a clashing sound.

clash.ety: Of onomatopoeic origin. Compare Saterland Frisian klatskje (“to smack, slap”), West Frisian kletse, kletskje, Dutch kletsen (“to smack, slap, clash”), German Low German klattsen, klatsken (“to smack, splash”), German klatschen (“to clap, smack, slap”) and Klatsch (“a clapping sound; the din resulting from two or more things colliding”), Danish klaske (“to clash, splatter”).

ex.en: The red shoes clash with this green shirt.
ex.ja: 赤い靴にこの緑のシャツとは似合わない。

ex.en: Japanese and American interests clashed on this point.
ex.ja: 日米の利害がこの点で衝突した。

ex.en: I think the shirt clashes with that red tie.
ex.ja: このシャツはその赤いネクタイとは合わないと思うわ。

note.ja: 擬音語。武器がぶつかり合う「ガチャン」という音 →「衝突・対立」。

zh: 相處融洽的 /相处融洽的

en: Capable of working together without conflict.
Able to get along well.
Something that is compatible with something else.

compatible.ety: Inherited from Middle English compatible, fron Anglo-Norman compatible, from Medieval Latin compatibilis (“in compatibile beneficium, a benefice which could be held together with another one”), from Late Latin compator (“to suffer with”), from com- (“together”) + pati (“to suffer”); see passion.

ex.en: They are very compatible.
ex.ja: 彼ら二人はよく肌が合う。

ex.en: My tape recorder is compatible with your amplifier.
ex.ja: 私のテープレコーダーは君のアンプにもつなげられる。

ex.en: Could you convert this file into a Windows 95 compatible file and re-send it?
ex.ja: このファイルをウインドウズ９５対応のファイルに変換して再送してくれますか。

note.ja: com（共に）+ pati（感じる・耐える）+ ble。共に耐えられる →「両立できる・互換性のある」。

en: Having received a curse to be doomed to suffer eternally.
Having been sharply scolded.
A person sentenced to death.

ex.en: He must be condemned for breaking his promise.
ex.ja: 彼は約束を破ったことで非難されなければならない。

ex.en: Whoever believes in him is not condemned.
ex.ja: 御子を信じるものは裁かれない。

ex.en: The accused was condemned to ten years in prison.
ex.ja: 被告は懲役１０年の刑を宣告された。

note.ja: condemn（有罪とする）+ -ed。con（完全に）+ damnare（罰する）。damn（呪う）も同じ。

en: The form of a thing, as depending on the relative placement of the parts of a thing's shape.
The relative positions of a set of things; the way things are arranged or put together;

configuration.ety: From Middle French configuration, from Latin cōnfigūrātiō. Morphologically configure + -ation.

ex.en: It is necessary to look more carefully into the demographic configuration of this region.
ex.ja: この地域の人口構成をもっと注意深く見ていく必要がある。

ex.en: We encounter similar difficulties when we substitute rectangles for triangles in this configuration.
ex.ja: この構成において、三角形の代わりに長方形を用いても類似の困難が生ずる。

note.ja: con（共に）+ figurare（形作る）+ -ation。「全体を形づくる配置」→「構成・設定」。figure（形・数字）と同じ。

en: Without pause.

continuously.ety:

Proto-Indo-European *leyg-der.

From continuous + -ly.

ex.en: The cost of living is going up continuously.
ex.ja: 生活費はいつも上がっている。

ex.en: The north wind blew continuously all day.
ex.ja: 北風は一日中吹き続けた。

ex.en: Prices are continuously rising.
ex.ja: 物価は上がり続けている。

note.ja: continuous（絶え間ない）+ -ly。con（共に）+ tenere（保つ）。「つなぎ保つ」→「続く」。continue と同じ。

en: Inquisitiveness; the tendency to ask and learn about things by asking questions, investigating, or exploring.
A unique or extraordinary object which arouses interest.

curiosity.ety: From Middle English curiosite, variant of curiouste, from Anglo-Norman curiouseté, from Latin cūriōsitātem, accusative of cūriōsitās. By surface analysis, curious + -ity. Displaced native Old English firwitt.

ex.en: You are really full of curiosity, aren't you?
ex.ja: 君は好奇心が旺盛だね。

ex.en: A healthy curiosity is truly a fine thing.
ex.ja: 好奇心がお旺盛なのは大変に結構なことである。

ex.en: I opened the box out of curiosity.
ex.ja: 好奇心から私はその箱を開けた。

note.ja: cur（注意・世話）+ ios + ity。注意を向けずにいられないこと →「好奇心・珍しいもの」。

Having the character of an explosion.
Any explosive substance.

ex.en: There has been an explosive increase in the demand for labor.
ex.ja: 労働需要の爆発的増加がみられてきた。

ex.en: Yanni had an explosive temper.
ex.ja: ヤニーは癇癪持ちだった。

note.ja: ex（外へ）+ plos（打つ）+ ive。外へはじけ出す →「爆発性の・爆薬・爆発的な」。

en: Auspicious.
Happening by good luck or favorable chance.

fortunate.ety: From Middle English fortunat(e) (“fortunate”), from Latin fortūnātus, from fortūna (“fortune, luck”) + -ātus (adjective-forming suffix), see -ate (adjective-forming suffix). See also Middle English fortunaten (“to assure the success (of), make fortunate”); cognate with French fortuné (“lucky”). By surface analysis, fortune + -ate.

ex.en: You are fortunate for having such good friends.
ex.ja: 君はこんなによい友人を持って幸運だ。

ex.en: The driver was so fortunate to escape death.
ex.ja: 運転していた人は幸運にも死を免れた。

ex.en: It is fortunate that you have such parents.
ex.ja: そんな両親をもって君は幸せだ。

note.ja: fortune（幸運）+ -ate。「幸運な」。

en: In a fortunate manner.
It is (or was, etc) fortunate that.

From fortunate + -ly.

ex.en: Fortunately, I've got you to talk to.
ex.ja: 運の良いことに、私には話しかけることができるあなたがいるのよ。

ex.en: Fortunately, I made it to the class.
ex.ja: 幸いにも授業に間に合った。

ex.en: Fortunately he didn't die in the accident.
ex.ja: 幸運にも彼は、その事故で死ななかった。

note.ja: fortunate（幸運な）+ -ly。ラテン語 fortuna（運・運命の女神）から。fortune（財産・運）。

en: The part of a country which borders or faces another country or unsettled region.
The most advanced or recent version of something; the leading edge.
To live as pioneers on frontier territory.

frontier.ety: From Middle English frounter, from Old French fronter (whence Modern French frontière), from front.

ex.en: Many families left to make a new life on the frontier.
ex.ja: 多くの家族が新生活を築くために辺境地方に移住した。

ex.en: The soldiers headed for the frontier with caution.
ex.ja: 兵士達は警戒しながら国境に向かって進んだ。

ex.en: Many families went west to make a new life on the frontier.
ex.ja: 多くの家族が辺境で新生活を始めるため西へ行った。

note.ja: front（前面）+ -ier。「前線にある地域」→「国境地帯・辺境・最先端」。front はラテン語 frons（額）。

en: Discouraging; causing annoyance or anger by excessive difficulty.

frustrating.ety:
Etymology tree
English frustrate
Middle English -ynge
English -ing
English frustrating
From frustrate + -ing.

ex.en: It was really frustrating.
ex.ja: 本当にいまいましかった。

ex.en: Ah! It's so frustrating not being able to keep up with everyone else.
ex.ja: あっ。みんなについていけない。イライラする！

ex.en: It's frustrating not being able to convey what I feel.
ex.ja: 気持ちを伝えれなくて、もどかしい。

note.ja: frustrate + -ing。「いらいらさせる」。

en: The feeling of annoyance at impossibility from resistance or inability to achieve something.
The act of frustrating, or the state, or an instance of being frustrated.

frustration.ety: From Latin frūstrātiō (“disappointment”), related to frūstrā (“in vain”). By surface analysis, frustrate + -ion.

ex.en: His anger was born of frustration.
ex.ja: 彼の怒りは欲求不満から生じた。

ex.en: Voters are taking out their frustrations at the polls.
ex.ja: 選挙民は投票によって不満をぶつけています。

ex.en: People react to the frustration in much the same way.
ex.ja: 人は欲求不満に対してほとんど同じように反応する。

note.ja: frustrate（挫折させる）+ -ation。ラテン語 frustra（むなしく）。「むなしくさせること」→「挫折・欲求不満」。

en: Pertaining to geography (or to geographics).
Determined by geography, as opposed to magnetic (i.e. North)

geographic.ety: From Latin geōgraphicus; see French géographique. By surface analysis, geography + -ic.

ex.en: The map shows the geographic features of the area.
ex.ja: その地図はその地域の地理的な特徴を示している。

note.ja: geo（大地）+ graph（描く）+ ic。地理の →「地理的な」。

en: To grip; to take hold, particularly with the hand.
To understand.
Grip.
Understanding.

grasp.ety:
From Middle English graspen, grapsen, craspen (“to grope; feel around”), from Old English *grǣpsian, from Proto-West Germanic *graipisōn, from Proto-Germanic *graipisōną, from Proto-Indo-European *gʰrebʰ- (“to take, seize, rake”), the same ultimate source as grab.
Cognate with Saterland Frisian grapsje (“to grab, grasp”), German Low German grapsen (“to grab; grasp”), German grapsen and grapschen, Old English grāpian ("to touch, feel, grasp"; > Modern English grope). Compare also Swedish krafsa (“to scatch; scabble”), Norwegian krafse (“to scramble”).

ex.en: I grasped the entire structure of his argument.
ex.ja: 私は彼の議論の全体像を把握した。

ex.en: We fail to grasp the meaning of the word.
ex.ja: 我々はその言葉の意味を理解できないでいる。

ex.en: The country is in the grasp of the enemy.
ex.ja: その国は敵の支配下にある。

note.ja: 中英語 graspen（手探りする）から。grab（つかむ）と同系。「つかむ」→ 頭でつかむ →「理解する」。

en: Easy to use, useful.
Nearby, within reach.
The hand.

handy.ety: From Middle English handy, hondi (attested in personal names), alteration of earlier hendi (“handy, skillful”), from Old English *hendiġ (“skillful”) (attested in listhendiġ (“skilled in art”)), from Proto-West Germanic *handīg, *handag, *handug, from Proto-Germanic *handugaz (“handy, skillful, nimble”), from *handuz (“hand”), equivalent to hand + -y. Cognate with Saterland Frisian jäntich (“handy”), Middle Low German handich (“skillful, apt”), Middle High German handec, hendec (“manual, hand-held”), Old Norse hǫndugr (“efficient”), Gothic 𐌷𐌰𐌽𐌳𐌿𐌲𐍃 (handugs, “wise, clever”). Akin to Dutch handi

ex.en: A car is a handy thing to own.
ex.ja: 車は持っていると重宝なものだ。

ex.en: I thought that this might come in handy.
ex.ja: これは役に立つかもしれないと思った。

ex.en: I thought this might come in handy.
ex.ja: これは役に立つかもしれないと思った。

note.ja: hand（手）+ -y。「手元にある」→「便利な・手近な・器用な」。

en: Having an extreme dedication to a certain activity.
So hard as to require extreme dedication to complete.
Broken bricks, stone and/or other aggregate used as foundations, especially in road and path laying.
Hardcore punk.
In a hardcore manner; intensely or extremely.

hardcore.ety: From hard + core: hard to the core; 1936 (n.); 1951 (adj.)

ex.en: He is a hardcore fan of the band.
ex.ja: 彼はそのバンドの筋金入りのファンだ。

note.ja: hard（固い）+ core（芯）。「固い芯」→「筋金入りの」。

en: Causing or likely to cause harm or damage; injurious.

harmful.ety:
From Middle English harmful, from Old English *hearmful (suggested by hearmfullīċ (“harmful; hurtful”)), equivalent to harm + -ful.
Cognate with German harmvoll, Danish harmfuld, Swedish harmfull.

ex.en: This medicine doesn't have any harmful side effects.
ex.ja: この薬には有害な副作用がありません。

ex.en: Smoking may be harmful to his heart.
ex.ja: 喫煙は彼の心臓によくないかもしれない。

ex.en: Playing cards is not in itself harmful.
ex.ja: トランプをすることはそれ自体に害はない。

note.ja: harm（害）+ -ful。古英語 hearm（悲しみ・害）。

en: A pain or ache in the head.
A nuisance or unpleasant problem.

headache.ety: From Middle English hevedeche, from Old English hēafodeċe. By surface analysis, head + ache.

ex.en: Tom told us that he had a headache.
ex.ja: トムは頭が痛いと私たちに言った。

ex.en: This medicine will take care of your headache.
ex.ja: この薬で君の頭痛は治るよ。

ex.en: Those college students give me a bad headache.
ex.ja: あの学生たちのことを考えると本当に頭痛の種だ。

note.ja: head（頭）+ ache（痛み）。「頭痛」→ 悩ませるもの →「頭痛の種」。toothache、stomachache と同じ作り。

en: Something that motivates, rouses, or encourages.
A bonus or reward, often monetary, to work harder.
Inciting; encouraging or moving; rousing to action; stimulating.
Serving to kindle or set on fire.

incentive.ety: From Medieval Latin incentīvus (“that strikes up or sets the tune”), from incinō (“to strike up”), from in- (“in, on”) + canō (“to sing”) + -ive. The formation appears to have been influenced by incendō (“to set on fire”).

ex.en: The workers have no incentive to work harder.
ex.ja: 労働者たちにはもっと働こうとする刺激がなにもない。

ex.en: Promotion was an incentive to harder work.
ex.ja: 昇進がより一層働く刺激となった。

ex.en: He was incensed by their lack of incentives.
ex.ja: 彼は彼らのやる気の無さに激怒した。

note.ja: ラテン語 incentivus（調子をつける）から。in + canere（歌う）。「歌でやる気を引き出す」→「動機・誘因」。chant（歌う）も同じ canere。

Including the extremes as well as the area between.

ex.ja: この表には過去の会員も含まれている。

ex.en: My total income is far short of 300,000 yen a month, inclusive of extra earnings.
ex.ja: 私の総収入は臨時収入を入れても月３０万円にはるか及ばない。

note.ja: include（含む）+ -sive。in + claudere（閉じる）。「中に閉じ込める」→「すべてを含んだ」。exclusive の対。

en: The state of being mad; insanity; mental disease.
The state of being angry.

madness.ety: From Middle English madnes, madnesse; equivalent to mad + -ness.

ex.en: It's the height of madness to say so.
ex.ja: そんなことを言うのは狂気のさただ。

ex.en: What he did was nothing less than madness.
ex.ja: 彼がしたことは狂気の沙汰としか言いようがなかった。

ex.en: His conduct was nothing short of madness.
ex.ja: 彼の行為はまさしく狂気の沙汰だった。

note.ja: mad（狂った）+ -ness。「狂気・ばかげたこと」。

en: An official or authoritative command; an order or injunction; a commission; a judicial precept; an authorization.
The order or authority to do something, as granted to a politician by the electorate.
To (officially) require someone to do something or act in a certain way, to give them the authority to do so; to command.
To make mandatory.

mandate.ety:
First attested in 1521; borrowed from Latin mandātum (“a charge, order, command, commission, injunction”), substantivized from the neuter forms of mandātus, perfect passive participle of mandō (“to commit to one's charge, order, command, commission, literally to put into one's hands”) (see -ate (noun-forming suffix)), from manus (“hand”) + -dere (“to put”).
Sense 3 in Canadian English is likely a semantic loan from French mandat.

ex.en: The new law mandates seat belts for all passengers.
ex.ja: 新しい法律はすべての乗客にシートベルトの着用を義務づけている。

note.ja: ラテン語 mandare（手に委ねる・命じる）から。manus（手）+ dare（与える）。「手に預ける」→「委任・権限・命令」。command、demand も同じ。

en: A comic originating in Japan.
An artistic style heavily used in, and associated with, Japanese comics, and that has also been adopted by a comparatively low number of …

Borrowed from Japanese 漫画(まんが) (manga), from Middle Chinese 漫 (MC manH, “free, unrestrained”) + 畫 (MC hweaH|hweak, “drawing”). Compare Mandarin 漫畫／漫画 (mànhuà), Korean 만화 (漫畵／漫畫, manhwa). After an 1814 book by Katsushika Hokusai. Doublet of manhua and manhwa.

ex.en: I learned everything important in life from mangas.
ex.ja: 人生で大切なことはすべて漫画から学んだ。

ex.en: This manga is pretty popular in China.
ex.ja: この漫画は中国でとても人気がある。

ex.en: The kid has a lot of mangas.
ex.ja: その子は漫画をいっぱい持ってるんだ。

note.ja: 日本語「漫画」がそのまま英語になった語。

en: Worthy to be remembered; very important or remarkable.
Something interesting enough to be remembered.

memorable.ety: From Middle English memorable, memorrable, from Latin memorābilis, from memorō (“to bring to remembrance”), from memor (“mindful, remembering”). By surface analysis, memory + -able, see memory. Doublet of memorabile (singular of memorabilia).

ex.en: This was a memorable day for me.
ex.ja: 記念すべき一日となりました。

ex.en: That'll make for a memorable time.
ex.ja: 貴重な思い出料としては安いものですよ。

ex.en: Dreams may be vivid and memorable.
ex.ja: 夢が生き生きと記憶に残ることもある。

note.ja: memory と同じラテン語 memorabilis（記憶すべき）から。「記憶に残る」。

ex.en: The tea leaves all point to a merger, if you ask me.
ex.ja: たぶん会社が合併するんじゃないかって思うんだけど。

en: A metal rod, generally of wrought iron, for adjusting the burning logs or coals in a fire; a firestick.
A tool like a soldering iron for making poker drawings.
To poke with a utensil such as a poker or needle.

ex.ja: 今まで一度もポーカーをやったことがないって、本当？

ex.en: He is very good at poker.
ex.ja: 彼はポーカーがとても上手だ。

note.ja: poke（つつく）+ -er。「火をつつく棒」→「火かき棒」。トランプのポーカーは別の語源とされる。

en: Able to be carried or easily moved.
Able to be transferred from one organization to another.
A trailer or other movable structure used for classes at a school.
A hand-held video gaming device.

portable.ety: From Middle English portable, from Middle French portable and Latin portābilis. By surface analysis, port (“to carry”) + -able.

ex.en: I buy a portable music player.
ex.ja: ポータブルな音楽プレイヤーを買う。

ex.en: Tom doesn't want an iPad. He wants a portable device that supports Flash.
ex.ja: トムはiPadは欲しくない。彼が欲しいのはFlashをサポートした携帯デバイスだ。

ex.en: I learned about your portable copier at the Tokyo-Office '97 Expo.
ex.ja: 貴社の小型コピー機を東京オフィス・エキスポ９７でしりました。

note.ja: ラテン語 portare（運ぶ）+ -able。「持ち運びできる」。port、transport と同じ。

en: In a random manner.
By random access; at any point at a given time; not sequentially.

ex.en: I randomly came up with this story in 33 minutes.
ex.ja: ３３分で口任せにこの話を仕上げました。

ex.en: This is a sentence that is being randomly displayed through Tatoeba.
ex.ja: この文はTatoebaにより無作為に表示されています。

note.ja: random + -ly。「無作為に」。

ex.en: He has something to do with the robbery.
ex.ja: 彼はその強盗事件と関係がある。

ex.en: He was sent to jail for the robbery.
ex.ja: 彼は強盗の罪で刑務所に送られた。

ex.en: Bank robbery will cost you ten years in prison.
ex.ja: 銀行強盗すると懲役１０年食らうぞ。

note.ja: rob（奪う）+ -ery。rob は古フランス語 rober から、ゲルマン系で「服をはぎ取る」。robe（長い衣服：はぎ取った戦利品）と同じ語源。

en: An act of rubbing.
A difficulty or problem.
To move (one object) while maintaining contact with another object over some area, with pressure and friction.
To be rubbed against something.

rub.ety:
Inherited from Middle English rubben, of unknown origin; possibly ultimately from Proto-Germanic *rubbōną, a hypothetical variant of *ruppōną (“to tear (off), rip; to wear away, rub”), related to *reufaną (“to tear”) (> English reave). If so, a doublet of rip.
Cognate with Saterland Frisian rubje (“to rub, scrape”), German Low German rubben (“to rub”), Low German rubblig (“rough, uneven”), Dutch robben, rubben (“to rub smooth; scrape; scrub”), Danish rubbe (“to rub, scrub”), Icelandic and Norwegian rubba (“to scrape”).
More at reave.
Compare typologically Latin fricō < friō < Proto-Indo-Europe

ex.en: Everything he says rubs me the wrong way.
ex.ja: 彼の言うことすべてが、私の神経を逆なでするのです。

ex.en: Never rub your eyes with dirty hands.
ex.ja: 汚れた手で目をこすってはいけません。

ex.en: The cat rubs its face against her.
ex.ja: ネコは彼女に顔をすりつける。

note.ja: 中英語 rubben から。北欧系とされる。「こする」。rubber（ゴム：鉛筆の跡をこすって消すもの）。

en: A willow.
Any tree that resembles a willow.
To make a sudden attack (e.g. on an enemy from a defended position).
To set out on an excursion; venture; depart (often followed by "forth").

sally.ety: From Middle English saly, from Old English saliġ, sealh (“willow”). More at sallow.

ex.en: Sally and I work in the same office.
ex.ja: サリーは職場の仲間です。

ex.en: Sally gave me a good piece of information.
ex.ja: サリーは私に良い情報を１つ教えてくれた。

ex.en: Sally made her brother clean the bathroom.
ex.ja: サリーは弟にバスルームを掃除させた。

note.ja: フランス語 saillie（飛び出し）から。ラテン語 salire（跳ぶ）。「城から飛び出す攻撃」→「出撃」、言葉が飛び出す →「気のきいた言葉」。

en: Dispersed, spread apart into disunited units.
Seemingly randomly distributed.

ex.en: Broken glass lay scattered all over the road.
ex.ja: ガラスの破片が、道路一面に散らばってたよ。

ex.en: The sudden noise scattered the birds.
ex.ja: 突然の物音に鳥たちは散り散りに飛び去った。

ex.en: The wind scattered the leaves about.
ex.ja: 風が葉を吹き散らした。

note.ja: scatter（まき散らす）+ -ed。shatter（粉々にする）と同系。「散らばった」→「まばらな」。

en: A person sent out to gather and bring back information; especially, one employed in war to gain information about the enemy and ground.
An act of scouting or reconnoitering.
To explore a wide terrain, as if on a search.
To observe, watch, or look for, as a scout; to follow for the purpose of observation, as a scout.

ex.en: When did you become a Boy Scout?
ex.ja: ボーイスカウトになったのはいつぐらい？

ex.en: The boy scouts went from door to door selling what they had made.
ex.ja: ボーイスカウトたちは自分たちの作った物を一軒一軒売ってまわった。

ex.en: The membership of the Boy Scout troop swelled.
ex.ja: ボーイスカウトの団員が増えた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 escouter（聞く）から。ラテン語 auscultare（耳を傾ける）。「耳をすませて偵察する人」→「偵察兵」→ 人材を探す →「スカウト」。

en: A blow, especially one given with the open hand, or with something broad and flat.
A sharp percussive sound like that produced by such a blow.
To strike someone, typically with an open hand, often on the face.
To cause something to strike soundly.
Exactly, precisely

slap.ety: From Middle English slappen, of uncertain origin, possibly imitative. Compare Low German Slappe (“slap”), whence also German Schlappe (“defeat”). Compare also Italian sleppa (“slap”).

ex.en: Slapped in the face, I didn't fight back.
ex.ja: 顔に平手打ちされたけれども、私は抵抗しなかった。

ex.en: Even so ... she didn't have to slap me!
ex.ja: だからって・・・なにもひっぱたくことないじゃないか。

ex.en: She gave him a slap in the face.
ex.ja: 彼女は彼の顔に平手打ちを食らわせた。

note.ja: 擬音語。「パチン」と平手でたたく音から。

en: Beefsteak: a slice of beef, broiled or cut for broiling.
A relatively large, thick slice or slab cut from another animal, a vegetable, etc.
To cook (something, especially fish) like or as a steak.

steak.ety:
From Middle English steike, from Old Norse steik (“roast; meat roasted on a stick”). The verb is either from the noun or from steikja (“to roast”).
The modern pronunciation shows an irregular change of Early Modern English /ɛː/ to /eɪ/ in the standard language; contrast this with the development of other words such as speak and wreak.

ex.en: Steak and red wine make a good combination.
ex.ja: ステーキと赤ワインはいい取り合わせだ。

ex.en: He ate up the steak and ordered another.
ex.ja: 彼はそのステーキを平らげてもう１つ注文した。

ex.en: Would you like to have steak for dinner?
ex.ja: 夜ご飯にステーキはどうですか？

note.ja: 北欧語 steik（焼いた肉）から。stick（棒）と同系で「串に刺して焼く」。

en: An act of following in sequence.
A sequence of things in order.

succession.ety: Inherited from Middle English [Term?], from Old French succession, from Latin successiō (noun).

ex.en: They won the Japan Cup three years in succession.
ex.ja: 彼らは３年連続してジャパン・カップに優勝した。

ex.en: After a succession of warm days, the weather became cold.
ex.ja: 暖かい日が連続した後、天候は寒くなった。

ex.en: He came to the throne by succession.
ex.ja: 彼は世襲によって王位についた。

note.ja: suc（次に）+ cess（進む）+ ion。次々に続くこと →「連続・継承」。

en: A person who is authorized to supervise, direct or administer something.
A police officer rank, positioned above chief inspector, and below chief superintendent.
Overseeing; superintending.

superintendent.ety: From Ecclesiastical Latin superintendens, a calque of Ancient Greek ἐπίσκοπος (epískopos); thence being distantly related to English bishop.

ex.en: The building superintendent fixed our heater.
ex.ja: 建物の管理人が暖房器具を直してくれた。

note.ja: super（上から）+ intendere（気を配る）+ -ent。「上から気を配る人」→「監督者・管理者」。intend と同じ。

en: The act of suspecting something or someone, especially of something wrong.
The condition of being suspected.

suspicion.ety: From Middle English suspecioun, borrowed from Latin suspīciō, suspīciōnem, from suspicere, from sub- (“up to”) with specere (“to look at”). Perhaps partly through the influence of Old French sospeçon (or rather the Anglo-Norman form suspecioun). Equivalent to suspect + -ion.

ex.en: He fell under the suspicion of the police.
ex.ja: 彼は警察の嫌疑を受けた。

ex.en: Her unusual behavior gave rise to our suspicions.
ex.ja: 彼女の異常な行動が私たちの疑いを引き起こした。

ex.en: The words confirmed him in his suspicions.
ex.ja: その言葉で彼に対する疑惑はさらに強まった。

note.ja: sub（下から）+ specere（見る）+ -ion。「下から（疑いの目で）見ること」→「疑い」。suspect、inspect も同じ specere。

en: To clean (a surface) by means of a stroking motion of a broom or brush.
To move through a (horizontal) arc or similar long stroke.
A single action of sweeping.
The person who steers a dragon boat.

sweep.ety: From Middle English swepen, from Proto-West Germanic *swaipijan (unattested in Old English), from Proto-Germanic *swaipijaną. Cognate with Early Modern West Frisian swiepe (“whip, cleanse, sweep”), from Old Frisian swēpa, suepa (“sweep”). More distantly related to Old Norse sveipa (whence Swedish svepa). See also swoop.

ex.en: The children were assigned to sweep the room.
ex.ja: 子供たちは部屋の掃除を割り当てられた。

ex.en: I would have somebody sweep this room clean.
ex.ja: 誰かにこの部屋を綺麗に掃除してもらいたい。

ex.en: A shadow of anxiety swept across her face.
ex.ja: 不安の影が彼女の顔をさっとよぎった。

note.ja: 古英語 swāpan（掃く）から。swoop（急降下する）と同系。「さっと払う」→「掃く・一掃する」。

A combinator of proof tactics.
A private war reenactment event involving mock battles or skirmishes.

note.ja: therapy（療法）+ -ist。ギリシャ語 therapeia（仕えること・治療）。「世話をする人」→「療法士・セラピスト」。

en: After that time, from then on; thenceforth.
After that (the thing aforementioned).
Synonym of hereafter (“future existence or state”).
Synonym of hereafter (“existence after death”).

thereafter.ety: From Middle English therafter, theraftir, þerefter, þerafter, þeræfter, from Old English þǣræfter (“after that; thereafter”), equivalent to there + after. Cognate with Saterland Frisian deerätter (“thereafter”), West Frisian dêrefter (“behind that; thereafter”), Dutch daarachter (“behind that; thereafter”), German Low German daarachter (“behind that”), Danish derefter (“thereafter”), Swedish därefter (“thereafter”).

ex.en: Thereafter we heard no more from him.
ex.ja: その後彼からは便りが無かった。

ex.en: Thereafter, he was gradually promoted until he became company president.
ex.ja: 彼はその後、累進して社長にまで進んだ。

note.ja: there（そこ）+ after（後に）。「その後」。thereby、therefore と同じ作り。

en: Painstaking and careful not to miss or omit any detail.
Utter; complete; absolute.

thorough.ety: From Middle English thoruȝ, þoruȝ, from Old English þuruh, a byform of Old English þurh, whence comes English through. The adjective derives from the preposition and adverb. The word developed a syllabic form in cases where the word was fully stressed: when it was used as an adverb, adjective, or noun, and less commonly when used as a preposition.

ex.en: He made a thorough analysis of the problem.
ex.ja: 彼はその問題を徹底的に分析した。

ex.en: The theory is based on thorough research.
ex.ja: その理論は周到な研究に基づいている。

ex.en: A thorough investigation is now in progress.
ex.ja: 詳しい調査は今進行中です。

note.ja: through（通して）の古い形。「端から端まで通した」→「徹底的な・完全な」。

en: The training or instruction provided by a teacher or tutor.
Paid private classes taken outside of formal education; tutoring. (also used attributively)

tuition.ety: From Anglo-Norman tuycioun, from Old French tuicion, from Latin tuitiō (“guard, protection, defense”), from tuēri (“to watch, guard, see, observe”). Compare intuition, tutor.

ex.en: They announced an increase in tuition fees.
ex.ja: 学校は授業料の値上げを発表した。

ex.en: I got a grant for my tuition.
ex.ja: 奨学金が交付された。

ex.en: I am working to save for my college tuition.
ex.ja: 大学の授業料をためるために働いています。

note.ja: ラテン語 tueri（見守る）から。「見守って教えること」→「指導」→ その費用 →「授業料」。tutor（家庭教師）も同じ。

en: An abnormal growth; differential diagnosis includes abscess, metaplasia, and neoplasia.

tumor.ety: From Middle English tumour, from Old French tumour, from Latin tumor (“swelling”), from tumeō (“bulge, swell”, verb), from Proto-Italic *tumēō, from Proto-Indo-European *tewh₂- (“to swell”). Related to English thumb.

ex.en: Tom had a brain tumor.
ex.ja: トムには脳腫瘍があった。

ex.en: I got a stomach tumor and had to have it operated on.
ex.ja: 胃に腫瘍ができたので切ってもらった。

ex.en: The tumor is growing.
ex.ja: 腫瘍は進行しています。

note.ja: ラテン語 tumere（腫れる）から。「腫れ」→「腫瘍」。

en: The sale of products, often in large quantities, to retailers or other merchants.
Of or relating to sale in large quantities, for resale.
Extensive, indiscriminate, all-encompassing; blanket.
In bulk or large quantity.
Indiscriminately.
To sell at wholesale.

ex.en: Wholesale prices are basically flat.
ex.ja: 卸売物価は基本的に安定している。

ex.en: A retail merchant buys wholesale and sells retail.
ex.ja: 小売商人は卸しで仕入れて小売りで売る。

ex.en: This morning, Mr Yamaha bought 30 kilos of walnuts wholesale.
ex.ja: 今朝、山羽さんが卸で胡桃を３０キロ買いました。

note.ja: whole（全体）+ sale（販売）。「まとめて全部売る」→「卸売り」→「大規模な」。

en: To apportion out, distribute.
To manage or supervise the conduct, performance or execution of; to govern or regulate the parameters for the conduct, performance or exe…

administer.ety: From Middle English administren, from Old French aminister, from Latin administrare (“to manage, execute”), from ad (“to”) + ministrare (“to attend, serve”), from minister (“servant”); see minister.

ex.en: The mayor administers the affairs of the city.
ex.ja: 市長は市政を司る。

ex.en: The doctor administered medicine to the patient.
ex.ja: 医者は患者に投薬した。

ex.en: The Secretary of State administers foreign affairs.
ex.ja: 国務長官は対外関係を統括する。

note.ja: ad（〜に）+ ministrare（仕える）。「人のために仕える」→「管理する・運営する・（薬を）投与する」。minister（大臣：仕える者）と同じ。

ex.ja: 遠くで大砲の音が聞こえた。

en: A type of coarse cloth, woven from hemp (traditionally) or from cotton and polyesters, useful for making sails, tents, and overcoats or a…
A piece of such cloth stretched across a frame on which one may paint an artwork.
To cover (an area or object) with canvas.

canvas.ety: From Middle English canevas, from Anglo-Norman, from Old Northern French canevas (compare Old French chanevas, chenevas) from a root derived from Latin cannabis, from Ancient Greek κάνναβις (kánnabis). Compare French canevas, resulting from a blend of the Old French and a Picard dialect word, itself from Old Northern French. Doublet of cannabis and hemp.

ex.en: This world is but canvas to our imaginations.
ex.ja: この世は我々の想像力にとっての画布そのものである。

ex.en: He swept his brush across the canvas.
ex.ja: 彼は絵筆をカンバスにさっと走らせた。

ex.en: Oil on canvas can never paint a petal so delicate.
ex.ja: キャンバスのオイルはとても微細な花びらを描けない。

en: A valley, especially a long, narrow, steep valley, cut in rock by a river.
Of water, liquid, or another substance, to flow in or into a canyon.

canyon.ety: Borrowed from Spanish cañón. Doublet of cannon.

ex.en: The Grand Canyon is one of the most popular places in the USA.
ex.ja: グランド・キャニオンはアメリカ有数の人気スポットだ。

ex.en: The Grand Canyon is the number one tourist attraction in America.
ex.ja: グランド・キャニオンはアメリカで一番人気のある観光スポットです。

note.ja: スペイン語 cañón（筒・管）から。caña（葦）+ 拡大の -ón。「大きな管のような谷」→「峡谷」。cannon と同系。

en: The soft skin on each side of the face, below the eyes; the outer surface of the sides of the oral cavity.
The lower part of the buttocks that is often exposed beneath very brief underwear, swimwear, or extremely short shorts.
To be impudent towards.
To pull a horse's head back toward the saddle using the cheek strap of the bridle.

cheek.ety:
From Middle English cheeke, cheke, cheoke, choke, from Old English ċēce, ċēace, ċēoce (“cheek; jaw”), from Proto-West Germanic *kākā, *keukā (“jaw, cheek”), from Proto-Germanic *kēkǭ, *keukǭ (“jaw; palate; pharynx”), perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *ǵyewh₁- (“to chew”).
Cognate with Saterland Frisian Sooke (“cheek”), West Frisian tsjeak (“jaw”), Dutch kaak (“jaw; cheek”), Swedish käke (“jaw; jowl”), Norwegian kjake (“jaw”), Old Norse kók (“mouth; gullet”).

ex.ja: ほっぺにキスしただけだろ。

ex.ja: トムはメアリーの両頬にキスをした。

ex.en: Mary gave me a kiss on the cheek.
ex.ja: メアリーがほっぺにちゅってしてくれた。

note.ja: 古英語 cēace（あご・頬）から。「頬」→ 頬をふくらませて言う生意気 →「生意気（なことば）」。

en: Of or relating to a circle.
In the shape of, or moving in, a circle.
An advertisement, directive or notice intended for mass circulation.
A shuttle bus with a circular route.
To distribute circulars to or at.
To extend in a circular direction.

circular.ety: From Middle English circuler, circuleer, circulere, from Old French circulier (French circulaire), from Late Latin circularis, from Latin circulus, diminutive of circus (“ring”). By surface analysis, circle + -ar.

ex.en: I put the circular in the post box.
ex.ja: ポストに回覧板入れといたよ。

ex.en: I put the circular in the mail box.
ex.ja: ポストに回覧板入れといたよ。

ex.en: I put the circular in the letter box.
ex.ja: ポストに回覧板入れといたよ。

note.ja: circle（円）+ -ar。ラテン語 circulus（小さな輪）。「円形の」→ 人々の間を回る →「回覧・ちらし」。

en: The act of moving in a circle, or in a course which brings the moving body to the place where its motion began.
The act of passing from place to place or person to person; free diffusion; transmission.

circulation.ety: From Middle English circulacioun, from Latin circulatio. Morphologically circulate + -ion.

ex.ja: 彼はこのごろ影を潜めてる。

ex.ja: その新聞は発行部数が多い。

ex.en: This paper has a large circulation.
ex.ja: この新聞は購読者が多い。

note.ja: circulate（循環する）+ -ation。「輪になって回ること」→「循環・流通・発行部数」。

The appearance of a meaningful connection between events when there is none.

coincidence.ety: From Middle French coincidence (French coïncidence). By surface analysis, coincide + -ence.

en: An entertainer who performs in a humorous manner, especially by telling jokes.
Any person who is humorous or amusing, either characteristically or on a particular occasion.

comedian.ety: From French comédien, from comédie + -ien, from Old French comedie, from Latin cōmoedia, from Ancient Greek κωμῳδία (kōmōidía). By surface analysis, comed(y) + -ian.

ex.ja: 彼女は歌手と言うよりはコメディアンだ。

ex.ja: あの喜劇役者は大変こっけいだ。

ex.ja: コメディアンは無惨な死や大事故といった悲劇的状況を冗談のネタにしている。

ex.ja: 私はその事ではやましく思っている。

ex.ja: トムは自分の心が潔白だと言っていた。

A note addressed to a patron or friend, prefixed to a work of art as a token of respect, esteem, or affection.

dedication.ety: Originated 1350–1400 from Middle English dedicacioun, from Old French dedicacion (“consecration of a church or chapel”), from Latin dēdicātiō, equivalent to dēdicātus+-iōn.

ex.ja: 一生懸命することは君に勝利をもたらす。

ex.ja: 私達はそのビルの落成式に出席しました。

ex.en: Office managers expect accuracy, efficiency, and dedication.
ex.ja: 仕事場の管理者は、正確さ、効率性、献身を期待する。

Confinement of a prisoner awaiting trial.

detention.ety: Borrowed from Middle French détention, from Latin detentio, detentionem. Equivalent to detain + -tion.

ex.ja: トムは授業中おしゃべりをしていたので居残りさせられた。

note.ja: 古英語に由来するゲルマン系の語。「雄のカモ」。duck は雌・総称。

en: To keep up, impose or bring into effect something, not necessarily by force.
To apply a rule or enforcement action to a person or user account.

enforce.ety: From Middle English enforcen, from Old French enforcier, from Late Latin infortiāre, from in- + fortis (“strong”).

ex.en: The government must enforce the law immediately.
ex.ja: 政府は法律を施行しなければならない。

ex.en: The law was enforced immediately.
ex.ja: その法律は直ちに実施された。

ex.en: The new law was enforced on the people of the island.
ex.ja: その島の住民に新しい法律が施行された。

note.ja: en（〜にする）+ forc（力）+ e。力をもたせる →「（法律などを）施行する・強いる」。

en: Very specific, clear, or detailed.
Containing material (e.g. language or film footage) that might be deemed offensive or graphic through clear and direct expressions.
The final few words of a text.

explicit.ety: Borrowed from French explicite, from Latin explicitus (“disentangled, easy”), variant of explicātus.

ex.en: I gave you explicit instructions not to touch anything.
ex.ja: 私はあなたに何にも触るなとはっきりと指示しました。

ex.en: He was explicit on the point.
ex.ja: 彼はその点をはっきり述べた。

ex.en: He was explicit in his instruction.
ex.ja: 彼の指示は明白だった。

note.ja: ex（外へ）+ plic（折る）+ it。折りたたまれたものを外へ広げた →「明白な・露骨な」。implicit（中に折り込まれた→暗黙の）と対。

en: In an explicit manner.

explicitly.ety:
Etymology tree
English explicit
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English explicitly
From explicit + -ly.

ex.en: The rules explicitly say that phones are not allowed.
ex.ja: 規則には携帯電話の使用は禁止とはっきり書かれている。

note.ja: explicit（明確な）+ -ly。ex（外へ）+ plicare（たたむ・折る）。「たたまれたものを広げた」→「はっきりと」。反対は implicit（中に折り込まれた → 暗黙の）。

en: Influenza.
Stomach flu.

ex.en: There's a lot of flu going around now.
ex.ja: 今インフルエンザが流行ってます。

ex.en: Did you receive your flu shot this season?
ex.ja: 今シーズン、インフルエンザの予防接種は受けましたか？

ex.en: Can we check the rapid spread of the 'flu?
ex.ja: 我々は流感の広がる速度を鈍らすことができるだろうか。

note.ja: influenza の短縮形。イタリア語 influenza（星の影響）から。昔、流行病は天体の影響と考えられた。influence と同じ。

en: Not allowed; specifically disallowed.

forbidden.ety: Past participle of the verb forbid. Doublet of verboten. Compare German verboten, Dutch verboden, Swedish förbjuden, and West Frisian ferbean.

ex.en: Students are forbidden to smoke on the school grounds.
ex.ja: その学校は構内での生徒たちの喫煙を禁止している。

ex.en: I am forbidden to use this telephone.
ex.ja: 私はこの電話を使うのを禁じられている。

ex.en: It is forbidden for you to touch that switch.
ex.ja: 絶対にそのスイッチに触ってはいけない。

note.ja: forbid（禁じる）の過去分詞。for（反対に）+ bid（命じる）。「しないよう命じる」→「禁じられた」。

en: A part of a whole, especially a comparatively small part.
A ratio of two numbers (numerator and denominator), usually written one above the other and separated by a horizontal bar called the vinc…
To divide or break into fractions.
To fractionate.

fraction.ety:
Etymology tree
Old French fraccionbor.
Middle English fraccioun
English fraction
From Middle English fraccioun (“a breaking”), from Anglo-Norman, Old French fraccion, from Medieval Latin fractio (“a fragment, portion”), from earlier Latin fractio (“a breaking, a breaking into pieces”), from fractus, past participle of frangere (“to break”) (whence English frangible), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰreg- (English break). Doublet of frazione.

ex.en: The fraction b/a means b times 1/a.
ex.ja: 分数b/aは1/aをb倍した数を意味する。

ex.en: He did it in only a fraction of a second.
ex.ja: 彼は１秒のほんの何分の１かでそれをした。

ex.en: Time is a certain fraction of eternity.
ex.ja: 時とは、永遠の一部分である。

note.ja: fract（壊す）+ ion。壊して分けたもの →「分数・ほんの一部」。fragile（壊れやすい）も同じ。

en: Soldiers who fight on foot (on land), as opposed to cavalry and other mounted units, regardless of external transport (e.g. airborne).
The part of an army consisting of infantry soldiers, especially opposed to mounted and technical troops.

infantry.ety: From Middle French infanterie, from older Italian, possibly from Spanish infantería (“foot soldiers, force composed of those too inexperienced or low in rank for cavalry”), from infante (“foot soldier”), originally "a youth", either way from Latin īnfāns (“child”); see there for more.

ex.en: The infantry soldier is only a pawn in the game of war.
ex.ja: 戦争の際には歩兵は取るに足らないものだ。

note.ja: イタリア語 infanteria から。infante（若者・歩兵）。ラテン語 infans（幼児）。若い兵士が歩兵だったことから。infant と同じ。

en: Constituting a whole together with other parts or factors; not omittable or removable.
Of, pertaining to, or being an integer.
One of the two fundamental operations of calculus (the other being differentiation), whereby a function's displacement, area, volume, or …
Any of several analytic formalizations of this operation: the Riemann integral, the Lebesgue integral, etc.

integral.ety: Borrowed from Middle French integral, from Medieval Latin integrālis, from Latin integer (“entire”); see integer.

ex.en: Music is an integral part of her life.
ex.ja: 音楽は彼女の生活に欠かせないものだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 integer（触れられていない→完全な）から。in（否定）+ teg（触れる）。欠けていない →「不可欠な・完全な」。

en: In a light manner.

lightly.ety: From Middle English lyghtly, liȝtliche, lihtliche, from Old English lēohtlīċe, equivalent to light + -ly.

ex.en: I dress lightly all the time.
ex.ja: 私はいつも薄着です。

ex.en: He took the reality of the situation lightly and failed.
ex.ja: 彼はその事実を軽く見て失敗した。

ex.en: If you go out so lightly dressed, you'll catch a cold.
ex.ja: そんな薄着で外出たら風邪引くよ。

note.ja: light（軽い）+ -ly。「軽く・軽々しく・そっと」。

en: A metamorphic rock of crystalline limestone.
A small ball used in games, originally of marble but now usually of glass or ceramic.
To cause (something to have) the streaked or swirled appearance of certain types of marble, for example by mixing viscous ingredients inc…
To get or have the streaked or swirled appearance of certain types of marble, for example due to the incomplete mixing of viscous ingredi…
Made of, or resembling, marble.
Cold; hard; unfeeling.

marble.ety: Inherited from Middle English marble, marbre; from Anglo-Norman and Old French marbre, from Latin marmor, from Ancient Greek μάρμαρος (mármaros), perhaps related to μαρμάρεος (marmáreos, “gleaming”). The forms from French displaced Old English marma, which had previously been borrowed from Latin.

ex.en: Her hands felt as cold as marble.
ex.ja: 彼女の手は冷たい大理石のような感じがした。

ex.en: He must have lost his marbles.
ex.ja: 彼はいかれちまったに違いない。

ex.en: The desk is made of marble.
ex.ja: その机は大理石でできてます。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 marmaros（輝く石）から。「大理石」→ 大理石で作った小さな玉 →「ビー玉」。

en: Relating to or connected with the sea or its uses (as navigation, commerce, etc.).
Bordering on the sea; living near the seacoast; coastal.

maritime.ety: Borrowed from Middle French maritime, from Latin maritimus.

ex.en: Japan is a maritime nation surrounded on all sides by ocean.
ex.ja: 日本は四方を海に囲まれた海洋国家です。

ex.en: Boeing developed a flying boat for the Maritime Self-Defense Force.
ex.ja: ボーイング社は海上自衛隊用の飛行艇を開発しました。

note.ja: ラテン語 maritimus（海の）から。mare（海）。「海の・海事の」。marine と同じ mar。

en: To change (or to be changed) from a solid state to a liquid state, usually by a gradual heat.
To dissolve, disperse, vanish.
Molten material, the product of melting.
The transition of matter from a solid state to a liquid state.

melt.ety: From Middle English melten, from a merger of Old English meltan (intransitive) and mieltan (transitive), both meaning “to melt, digest,” from Proto-West Germanic *meltan and *maltijan, from Proto-Germanic *meltaną and *maltijaną, both from Proto-Indo-European *(s)meld- (“melt”). Cognate with Icelandic melta (“to digest”).

ex.en: Ice turns back into water when it melts.
ex.ja: 氷は解けると水に戻る。

ex.en: I think that the snow will melt soon.
ex.ja: 雪はすぐに解けると思いますよ。

ex.en: America is often referred to as a melting pot.
ex.ja: アメリカはしばしばるつぼと言われる。

note.ja: 古英語 meltan（溶ける）から。smelt（精錬する）、malt（麦芽）と同系。「溶ける」→ 心が溶ける →「和らぐ」。

en: A person named, or designated, by another, to any office, duty, or position; one nominated, or proposed, by others for office or for elec…
A person or organisation in whose name a security is registered though true ownership is held by another party, called nominator, especia…

ex.en: She was a nominee for the best actress award.
ex.ja: 彼女は主演女優賞の候補者だった。

note.ja: nominate（指名する）+ -ee（〜される人）。「指名された人・候補者」。

en: A solemn pledge or promise that invokes a deity, a ruler, or another entity (not necessarily present) to attest the truth of a statement …
A statement or promise which is strengthened (affirmed) by such a pledge.

oath.ety:
From Middle English ooth, oth, ath, from Old English āþ (“oath”), from Proto-West Germanic *aiþ (“oath”), from Proto-Germanic *aiþaz (“oath”).
Cognate with Scots aith, athe (“oath”), North Frisian ith, iss (“oath”), Saterland Frisian Eed (“oath”), West Frisian eed (“oath”), Dutch eed (“oath”), German Eid (“oath”), Swedish ed (“oath”), Icelandic eið (“oath”), Latin ūtor (“make use of, employ, avail”, verb), Old Irish óeth (“oath”).

ex.en: She gave her oath that she would not drink.
ex.ja: 彼女は酒をやめると誓った。

ex.en: I will read the athletes' oath at sports day.
ex.ja: 僕、運動会で選手宣誓するんだ。

ex.en: He said under oath that he was born in Italy.
ex.ja: 彼は出生地は確かにイタリアだと誓った。

note.ja: 古英語 āth（誓い）から。ドイツ語 Eid と同じゲルマン系の語。

en: A person who loves and zealously supports and defends their country.

patriot.ety: From Middle French patriote, from Late Latin patriōta (“fellow countryman”) from the Ancient Greek πατριώτης (patriṓtēs, “of the same country”), from πατρίς (patrís, “father land", "country”), from πατήρ (patḗr, “father”).

ex.en: No man can be a patriot on an empty stomach.
ex.ja: 何人も空の胃の腑では愛国者たり得ない。

ex.en: The patriots stood up for the rights of their nation.
ex.ja: 愛国者達は国民の権利を擁護した。

ex.en: The patriot sticks to his moral principles.
ex.ja: その愛国者は自分の道徳的な信条を曲げない。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 patriotes（同じ祖国の人）から。patr（父）。父祖の国を愛する人 →「愛国者」。

en: Urine.
An act of urination.
To urinate.
To urinate on oneself.

pee.ety: The initial letter of piss. Compare eff.

ex.en: With practice, even girls can pee standing up.
ex.ja: 訓練すれば、女の子だって立っておしっこできます。

ex.en: Can I go to the bathroom? I need to pee.
ex.ja: トイレに行ってもいい？おしっこしたい。

ex.en: Does it hurt when you pee?
ex.ja: おしっこをすると痛みがありますか？

note.ja: piss の頭文字 p を発音した婉曲語。

en: A soft cushion used to support the head in bed.
Any similar head support used for sleep, such as a neck pillow or a hard porcelain pillow.
To rest as on a pillow.

pillow.ety:
From Middle English pilwe, from Old English pyle, pylu (“pillow”), from Proto-West Germanic *pulwī (“pillow”), from Latin pulvīnus (“cushion”), derived from pulvis (“dust”), for the filler of a pillow. Doublet of pulvinus.
Cognate with Saterland Frisian Peel (“pillow”), Alemannic German Pfulme (“pillow”), Dutch peluw (“a long, narrow pillow”), German Pfühl (“a big and soft pillow”), German Low German Pöhl (“pad, pillow, cushion”).

ex.en: She laid her head down on the pillow.
ex.ja: 彼女は頭を枕にのせた。

ex.en: Tom decided to try sleeping without a pillow.
ex.ja: トムは枕なしで眠ろうと決めた。

ex.en: He laid his head on the pillow.
ex.ja: 彼は枕に頭を横たえた。

note.ja: ラテン語 pulvinus（クッション）から古英語に入った語。

en: Of, relating to, measured from, or referred to a geographic pole (the North Pole or South Pole); within the Arctic or Antarctic circles.
Of an orbit that passes over, or near, one of these poles.
The line joining the points of contact of tangents drawn to meet a curve from a point called the pole of the line.

ex.ja: 昨日ね、シロクマを見たの。

ex.en: Take a moment to imagine what the polar bear's environment is like.
ex.ja: 北極熊の環境がどのようなものか、ちょっと想像してほしい。

ex.en: Polar bears live in the Arctic.
ex.ja: シロクマは北極地方に住んでいる。

note.ja: pole（極）+ -ar。「極地の」→ 両極のように「正反対の」。

en: A statement of what will happen in the future.
A probability estimation based on statistical methods.

prediction.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin praedictiō, praedictiōnis; equivalent to predict + -ion. Compare the Germanic equivalents forespeaking, foretale, foretelling.

ex.en: Strange to say, his prediction has come true.
ex.ja: 不思議な話だが、彼の予言は当たった。

ex.en: I'm afraid your prediction was wide of the mark.
ex.ja: 残念ながら、あなたの予測は的外れでした。

ex.en: To our surprise, her prediction came true.
ex.ja: 私たちが驚いたことに、彼女の予言が的中した。

note.ja: pre（前もって）+ dict（言う）+ ion。前もって言うこと →「予言・予測」。

en: An experience of something in advance.
An advance showing of a film, exhibition etc.
To show or watch something, or part of it, before it is complete.
To show something in advance, a facility for viewing and checking a document or photo, or changes to it, before saving or printing it.

preview.ety: From pre- + view; compare Old French preveü, past participle of preveoir (“to foresee”).

ex.en: There was a special sneak preview last night.
ex.ja: 昨日の夜、特別試写会があった。

note.ja: pre（前もって）+ view（見る）。「前もって見ること」→「下見・試写」。review（振り返って見る）と対。

ex.ja: そのパズルを解くのは難しかった。

ex.en: The solution of the puzzle required no time.
ex.ja: そのパズルを解くのに時間はかからなかった。

note.ja: 語源は不詳。16世紀ごろから「困らせる」→「難問・パズル」。

en: The knocker of a door.
A swinging knocker for making signals at the mouth of a shaft.

en: The action of reconstructing something, not necessarily to the earlier state.
The act of restoring something to an earlier state.

From re- + construction.

ex.en: Benefits accrue to the community from reconstruction.
ex.ja: 再開発によって地域に便益が生ずる。

en: Famous, celebrated, or well-known; widely praised or highly honored.

ex.en: The country is renowned for the beauty of its mountain scenery.
ex.ja: その国は山の景色が美しいので有名です。

note.ja: renown（名声）+ -ed。re（繰り返し）+ nommer（名を呼ぶ）。「何度も名を呼ばれる」→「有名な」。noun、name と同系。

en: The act of revealing or disclosing.
Something that is revealed.

revelation.ety: From Middle English revelacioun, from Old French revelacion, from Latin revēlātiō (“disclosure”), from revēlō (“to disclose”), re (“again”) + vēlō (“to cover”); by surface analysis, revelate + -ion.

ex.en: It was a revelation to me.
ex.ja: それは私にとって意外な話だった。

ex.en: His extensive knowledge of music was a revelation to us.
ex.ja: 彼が音楽について大変詳しいのは我々にとって意外なことでした。

note.ja: reveal（明らかにする）+ -ation。re（反対に）+ velare（ベールで覆う）。「ベールを取ること」→「暴露・啓示」。veil（ベール）。

en: A separate article of clothing, usually worn by women and girls, that hangs from the waist and covers the lower torso and part of the legs.
A similar part of a dress or robe, etc., that hangs below the waist.
To be on or form the border of.
To move around or along the border of; to avoid the center of.

ex.en: Long skirts were in fashion in those days.
ex.ja: その頃、ロングスカートが流行していた。

In social contexts.

ex.ja: 彼は内気だが、人付き合いはうまい。

en: A health resort near a mineral spring or hot spring.
A trendy or fashionable resort.

spa.ety: The term is derived from the name of the Belgian town of Spa, where since medieval times illnesses caused by iron deficiency were treated by drinking chalybeate (iron-bearing) spring water. In 16ᵗʰ century England the old Roman ideas of medicinal bathing were revived at towns like Bath, and in 1571 William Slingsby who had been to the Belgian town (which he called Spaw) discovered a chalybeate spring in Yorkshire. He built an enclosed well at what became known as Harrogate, the first resort in England for drinking medicinal waters, then in 1596 Dr. Timothy Bright called the resort The English

ex.en: I hit on a spa.
ex.ja: 僕は偶然温泉を見つけた。

ex.en: The outdoor spa at this hot spring is wonderful.
ex.ja: この旅館は露天風呂がすばらしいのよ。

note.ja: ベルギーの温泉町 Spa の名前から。「温泉・保養地」。

en: A sort of very large nail.
A piece of pointed metal etc. set with points upward or outward.
To fasten with spikes, or long, large nails.
To set or furnish with spikes.

spike.ety: From Middle English spike, spyke, spik, from Old Norse spík (“spike, sprig”), from Proto-Germanic *spīkō (“stick, splinter, point”), from Proto-Indo-European *spey- (“to be pointed; sharp point, stick”).
